instruction: I have a zipped Chrome extension on the Desktop that needs to be installed. Please extract it and load the unpacked extension from the Desktop/helloExtension folder into Chrome.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

rules.description: Verifies both folder extraction and Chrome extension installation
required_checks: folder_exists: Extension folder must exist at /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension
extension_installed: Extension must be loaded into Chrome (verified via Preferences file)

postconfig.description: Navigate to chrome://extensions to ensure UI is ready for verification

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting and installing an unpacked Chrome extension. The evaluator verifies that the extension folder exists at /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension. Custom getter checks folder existence using bash command on VM. Metric returns 1.0 if folder exists.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete verification coverage: Evaluator correctly verifies BOTH requirements (1. folder extraction via folder_exists check, 2. Chrome extension installation via Preferences file check)
Correct getter logic: Getter checks folder existence using bash command AND verifies extension is loaded by reading Chrome Preferences file (/home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences)
Correct metric logic: Metric returns 1.0 only when BOTH folder_exists=True AND extension_installed=True, correctly implementing conjunctive verification
Robust implementation: Getter handles different OS types (Windows, Darwin, Linux) with appropriate Preferences file paths
State accessibility: Chrome Preferences file is accessible post-task execution and reliably indicates extension installation status
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor optimization: The postconfig navigates to chrome://extensions but the getter doesn't use the page content (it reads Preferences file directly). The postconfig could be removed unless needed for other reasons.
Consider adding expected.rules.extension_name or extension_id to verify the correct extension was loaded (current implementation just checks if folder path appears in any extension)
